title: Ludwig Camerarius's letters from The Hague in his numeric code: several letters with no decipherment
correspondents: Ludwig Camerarius (Palatine councillor, Swedish resident and later ambassador at The Hague) -> Gustav II Adolf, and -> Johan Skytte ("Vir amice")
language: Latin (numeric nomenclator: 2-4 digit code groups, groups below about 100 for single letters)
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Hollandica, SE/RA/2109/I/5/7 (Residenten, slutligen ambassadören, Ludwig Camerarius, Brev till Kungl. Maj:t 1626-1628, 1630; also letters to Johan Skytte)
folio_note: 535 images (series R0003234). Bare cipher: 426 (`Cl. vir, amice singularis`), 432 (`S.P. Vir amice obs.`, Sept 1630), 442 (`Serenissime Rex`, a full page of code), 460 (both pages). 428 is bare but duplicates the glossed 427. Glossed (decipherment above the numbers): 109, 427, 498; 215 is a second system (digits run together with signs and letters, `/q` `/b` suffixes), glossed. More cipher at 73, 144, 423, 451 (not zoomed). Only about 45 of 535 images seen.
status: Catalogue: volume title only, no mention of cipher. Bare at 2400 px on 426, 432, 442, 460 (428 at 3200 px): no interlinear or marginal decipherment, and no deciphered copy on the facing images 424-432 except for 427/428 (two copies of one letter, one glossed). Other letters in the volume carry Latin decipherments above the numbers, so a key can be rebuilt from the glossed pairs. The system looks like the one-part nomenclator of Camerarius's 1621-22 Munich letters (target camerarius1621: 2-4 digit groups in plaintext order, low numbers spelling letters, homophones for frequent words).
why: Gustav Adolf's agent at The Hague in the years before the Swedish landing in Germany (1626-30), reporting on the Palatine cause, the Dutch, England and the Empire: a dated Latin code corpus with its own key material in the same volume, and some letters never deciphered on the page.
verify: Page the whole volume and list every ciphered letter, glossed or bare; transcribe the glossed letters (109, 427, 498 ...) and build the code list; test it on 426, 432, 442, 460; compare with targets/camerarius1621/key.tsv and with the Camerarius-docket letter riksarkivet4284 (1628, catalogue #207 family). Check Schubert, Ludwig Camerarius (1955) and the Camerariana in Munich for drafts or decipherments.
prior_art: known.py: no hit on the shelfmark; Camerarius appears only as the 1621-22 Munich target (camerarius1621, in progress) and as a docket on riksarkivet4284 (Oxenstierna collection, 1628). No edition of the Stockholm letters checked; DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry not searched

title: Consul Peter Christian Wulff's despatches from Salé: unbroken digit-string cipher with no decipherment
correspondents: Peter Christian Wulff (Swedish consul at Salé, Morocco) -> the Kanslipresident and Kanslikollegium (Stockholm)
language: Swedish (cipher text numeric, digits run together without separators)
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Maroccana, SE/RA/2112/II/I (Konsuln Peter Christian Wulff i Salé, 1764-1775; also letters from the courier Andr. Stenbeck 1770-71)
folio_note: 167 images (series R0003632). Cipher: 11 (two blocks of digit rows), 12 (two full pages of digits), 13 (one full page), 14, 18 and 24 (digit lines inside the clear text). Letters of 1764-66 (Salé 21 April 1764 at 10). Later letters (48-167) clear on the sample. About 45 of 167 images seen.
status: Catalogue: consul's letters, no mention of cipher. **No decipherment seen** on 12 (3000 px), 13, 18, 24 (2400 px) or 11, 14 (700 px): nothing above or below the digit rows, and the clear lines around 14, 18, 24 carry on the letter's own text. The same string 4471683745073806223843 stands before `presenterne` in 18 and 24 (a phrase about the peace presents for the Sultan): a crib. Written in the same way as consul Molinari's Tunis cipher of 1765-70 (lead 2260, held): probably the Kanslikollegium's consular code of the 1760s.
why: Sweden's first consul in Morocco during the 1763 peace treaty and the delivery of the peace presents: an unglossed 1760s consular code that likely matches the Tunis lead, so the two can be attacked together.
verify: Page 2-50 for every cipher passage and any key slip or deciphered copy; measure the digit strings for the group length (2- or 3-digit); compare digit statistics with Molinari (Tunisica 7/2, lead 2260); look for the consular code in Riksarkivet's cipher collections (Kanslikollegium chifferböcker) and in the Kanslikollegium registry copies of the replies to Wulff.
prior_art: known.py: no hit on the shelfmark or on Wulff. Related lead 2260 (Molinari, Tunis) is held pending Jerad's 2015 edition; no edition of Wulff's letters found. DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry not searched

folio_note: Hollandica 26/301: 189 images (series 40006086), cipher at 89, 152. Anglica 26/214: 153 images (series 40006088), cipher at 133.
